hypothesis: A learned token-query association term improves paired last-write retrieval and transfer to unseen names, relative to otherwise identical query-blind memory pointer.
scope: Narrow learned byte-memory circuit alongside the existing L100EC 100M parent; not general free-text LM improvement; this run does not fine-tune the 100M backbone
child_circuit: 16d ASCII embedding, 48 hidden learned structural scorer, query-to-record embedding-distance term, learned recency
control_difference: matching term multiplied by zero, with other trainable components and seeds identical; intentionally query-blind ablation
train_target: first digit position for last matching update (supervised source position); inference sees prompt bytes only
primary_metric: both retrieved values correct when query switches on the same unchanged memory bank
success: at least +10 percentage points over query-blind on held IID pairs, paired bootstrap 95 percent lower bound above zero; baseline quality and all other splits disclosed
postselection: None; train fixed 1024 steps, evaluate once at fixed endpoint, no held-based hyperparameter tuning
limits: Exact byte serializer: one-letter ASCII keys; equals records separated by semicolon; question mark followed by queried key; copy digits. No natural RU/EN/code benchmark, no Qwen parity, no tool-free universal LM improvement.
host: CPU-only 5 vCPU approx 5.8GiB RAM; RTX3090 inaccessible
